# Chapter 01 - The Sealed Copy

The copied record could clear the accused archivist.

It could also drag the courier, the clerk, and the unnamed wood supplier back into the hearing room before anyone had protection in place.

The investigator held the page above the table and did not put it down.

"If I file this now, who gets questioned first?"

No one answered.

The senior reviewer looked at the copied seal, then at the door. Outside, two guards were already waiting for the courier.

The page felt light enough to tear. It was not light in her hand.

She folded the copy once and kept it in her sleeve.

"Source unclear," she said. "Not ready for live filing."

The accused archivist did not thank her. His face only changed for one breath, as if he had hoped she would save him loudly and feared she would.

By keeping the page back, she had saved the helpers for one more hour.

By keeping it back, she had also left him under the old charge.
